title: Alpine Skiing
description: Signature alpine skiing is taught as turn shape before speed. A student learns to stop, then to turn, then to link turns, on a gentle slope, before any steep run, because speed control lives in the shape of the turn, not in braking. Our instructors teach carving as a quiet edge change, and they film students from the side so each skier can see whether their skis are truly parallel. Racing comes only when linked turns are reliable, and the hall's praise goes to the skier whose turns are round and calm at any speed.

demo.code:
DAYS = [('Monday stopping and turning', 90), ('Wednesday linked turns', 90), ('Friday carving drills', 90), ('Sunday guided slope skiing', 120)]
print('Signature alpine skiing learning week')
total = sum(m for _, m in DAYS)
best = max(DAYS, key=lambda d: d[1])
for day, m in DAYS:
    print('%s: %d minutes' % (day, m))
print('Weekly total: %d minutes' % total)
print('Daily average: %.1f minutes' % (total / len(DAYS)))
print('Longest session: %s (%d minutes)' % (best[0], best[1]))
demo.expected_output:
Signature alpine skiing learning week
Monday stopping and turning: 90 minutes
Wednesday linked turns: 90 minutes
Friday carving drills: 90 minutes
Sunday guided slope skiing: 120 minutes
Weekly total: 390 minutes
Daily average: 97.5 minutes
Longest session: Sunday guided slope skiing (120 minutes)

training: Sessions pair stopping drills, single turns, linked turns, and video review from the side.
techniques: Signature basics are stopping, turning, linking turns, and carving through edge change.
safety: Helmets are always worn, bindings are checked, and off-piste skiing requires avalanche training.
history: The Signature school follows alpine skiing from Alpine travel to resort sport and Olympic racing.

title: Cross-Country Skiing
description: Signature cross-country skiing is taught as glide before effort. A student learns to balance on one ski and glide, then to add the pole plant, then to link strides, because a skier who cannot glide wastes every push. Our programme teaches classic technique first, since the track guides the ski, and skate technique only when balance is reliable. Waxing is taught as a practical skill from the first month, and long skis build slowly, adding distance week by week. The hall's praise goes to the skier whose stride looks effortless after an hour, not the skier who starts fastest.

print('Pace: %.2f minutes per km' % pace)
print('Average speed: %.2f km per hour' % speed)

training: Sessions pair balance and glide drills, classic technique, skate technique, and gradually longer skis.
techniques: Signature basics are the glide, the pole plant, the diagonal stride, and double poling.
safety: Layers and weather checks are standard, skiers carry a phone and food on long outings, and groups stay together.
history: The Signature school follows the sport from Scandinavian winter travel to Olympic racing.

title: Ski Jumping
description: Signature ski jumping is taught as a landing before a flight. A student practises the telemark landing on flat ground, then from small jumps, and only then on a small hill, because a jump is only as good as its landing. Our coaches teach the inrun crouch as stillness, not speed, and the take-off as a forward lean timed to the table's edge. Flight position is built in stages, and hill size rises only when landings are consistently clean. The hall's praise goes to the jumper whose landing is quiet and balanced, whatever the distance.

print('Passed: %d of %d' % (passed, len(CHECKS)))

techniques: Signature basics are the crouch, the take-off lean, the V-style flight, and the telemark landing.
safety: Hill size rises only when landings are clean, and coaches supervise every jump.
history: The Signature school follows ski jumping from nineteenth-century Norway to the Four Hills Tournament.

title: Snowboarding
description: Signature snowboarding is taught as edge before air. A student learns to stop on each edge, then to link turns, then to carve, on a gentle slope, before any park feature is attempted, because every trick rests on edge control. Our instructors teach falling safely, with wrists protected and arms tucked, as a first lesson, so that falls stop being frightening. Park features are progressed by size, from small boxes to jumps, and only when riding is reliable. The hall's praise goes to the rider whose turns are smooth and whose landings are quiet.

title: Biathlon
description: Signature biathlon is taught as stillness inside speed. A student learns to ski, then to shoot, then to combine them, and the range routine is drilled until it survives a racing heart: ski in, settle, breathe out, shoot, leave. Our programme teaches shooting on the range only, with strict handling rules, and penalty loops are practised as part of racing, not as punishment. Breathing control is trained deliberately, since the last breath before a shot decides it. The hall's praise goes to the athlete who shoots clean after skiing hard, because that is the whole sport in one moment.

title: Bobsleigh
description: Signature bobsleigh is taught as a start before a slide. A crew practises the push on dry land until every step lands together, then loads into a stationary sled, then runs a slow track, because a fast sled with a poor start is already beaten. Our programme teaches steering as small, early movements, since late steering on ice only makes the sled swing wider. Braking is drilled as seriously as pushing, and the hall's praise goes to the crew whose start is silent and together, with no wasted step.

title: Luge
description: Signature luge is taught as stillness at speed. A student learns the lying position on a dry sled, then the paddling start, then slow-track runs, because any movement on the sled at speed changes its line. Our coaches teach steering as pressure, not as turning: a small leg press, a small shoulder press, and the sled answers. Doubles pairs practise lying together on dry land until the pair moves as one body. The hall's praise goes to the slider whose run looks motionless, because stillness is what speed rewards.

title: Skeleton
description: Signature skeleton is taught as a dive before a slide. A student practises the sprint and dive onto a stationary sled until the movement is automatic, then runs slow tracks, because a poor dive ruins the run before the first curve. Our coaches teach steering as weight, not as wrestling: a shift of the shoulders, a drag of the toe, and the sled follows. Head-first position is built gradually, with neck strength work, and the hall's praise goes to the slider whose dive is quiet and whose run is calm.

title: Speed Skating
description: Signature speed skating is taught as position before power. A student learns the deep crouch on dry land, then the side push on ice at low speed, then cornering, because power added to a poor position only wastes energy. Our coaches film skaters from the side so each athlete can see whether their crouch holds through a lap, and long skates build slowly, since endurance in the crouch is the sport's hidden demand. The hall's praise goes to the skater whose position never rises, even in the last lap.

title: Short-Track Speed Skating
description: Signature short-track is taught as pack awareness before passing. A student learns to skate in a group, to hold a line through corners, and to read when a gap opens, before any passing is attempted, because a pass attempted blind is a fall for two skaters. Our sessions drill relay exchanges by push until the exchange is smooth at speed, and disqualification rules are taught as tactics: knowing what is illegal keeps a skater in the race. The hall's praise goes to the skater who passes cleanly and leaves room, not the skater who forces a gap.

title: Figure Skating
description: Signature figure skating is taught as edges before jumps. A student learns to hold an edge, to turn cleanly, and to spin upright, before any jump is attempted, because a jump launched from a poor edge cannot be landed well. Our programme pairs ice sessions with ballet and off-ice jump training, and programmes are built one element at a time, with music chosen after the elements are solid. Falls are treated as information, not failure, and the hall's praise goes to the skater whose programme flows as one piece, not as a list of tricks.

title: Curling
description: Signature curling is taught as weight before strategy. A student learns to slide and release a stone with consistent weight, then to sweep, then to call simple shots, because strategy built on unreliable weight is only guessing. Our programme teaches sweeping as judgement: sweepers watch the stone's line and speed and decide together, rather than sweeping on every shot. The skip's role is taught as communication, not command, and the hall's praise goes to the team whose stones finish where they were called, end after end.

A student learns to land from small jumps, then to spin on a trampoline, then to take a trick to a water ramp, and only then to snow, because a trick learned on snow first is learned with fear. Our coaches teach mogul turns as short, round, and quiet, and aerials as height first and rotation second, since height gives time to land well. The hall's praise goes to the skier whose landing is balanced and whose run flows, whatever the trick's difficulty.

title: Ski Mountaineering
description: Signature ski mountaineering is taught as a mountain decision before a mountain climb. A student learns to read a forecast, to test snow, and to turn back, before any summit is attempted, because the mountain does not reward persistence. Our programme teaches skinning and kick turns on gentle slopes, transitions until they are fast and calm, and descending in varied snow, in that order. Avalanche training comes first, not last, and every tour carries transceiver, shovel, and probe, with the group practising rescue before the season. The hall's praise goes to the party that returns safely, whatever the summit.

title: Ice Climbing
description: Signature ice climbing is taught as placement before power. A student learns to swing an axe once and place it cleanly, to set crampon points without kicking wildly, and to rest on straight arms, on an indoor wall, before any frozen waterfall is attempted. Our instructors teach reading ice as a first skill: soft ice takes a gentle swing, brittle ice takes patience, and bad ice means no climb. Rope skills and rescue are taught beside climbing, not after it, and the hall's praise goes to the climber whose swings are few and whose movement is calm.

title: Snowshoeing
description: Signature snowshoeing is taught as walking, then winter. A student learns to fit bindings, to walk with a wider gait, and to turn without tripping, on flat ground, before any trail is attempted, because snowshoes punish a normal walking stride. Our programme teaches climbing with toe crampons, descending with short steps, and breaking trail in turns, so the group shares the hardest work. Navigation and layers are taught from the first outing, and the hall's praise goes to the walker who finishes warm, dry, and unhurried, whatever the distance.
